featured_reviews.review_text: Visited Persian Darbar, Bandra and had Lebanese chicken tikka, galauti kebab, mutton chop, mutton roghan josh, and chicken tikka masala. The starters were absolutely superb and easily deserve 5 stars. The main course was also quite good, especially the mutton roghan josh, though I would rate it 4 stars. The ambience is a bit old-fashioned, but the service was prompt and courteous. I visited once for dinner and once for lunch, and both times the bill for three people was around ₹1650, which felt reasonable for the quality and quantity served. Overall, a good place for great kebabs and starters.

featured_reviews.name: Vinita Nair
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our all time go to for the best biryani in Mumbai. All biryani lovers should try this place. They also have the best Chinese.
We ordered for Persian special biryani, Lebanese chicken tikka, caramel custard and kunafa.
All were delicious and are highly recommended dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Fazal Khan
featured_reviews.review_text: We have visited this restaurant many times, but this time I decided to share a review. The food at Persian Darbar is truly delightful and good ambiance. Although the service could be a bit better, the taste of the dishes more than makes up for it. The must-try item here is the 3-in-1 Raan, which is perfect for a group of six. For couples, the Chicken Tandoori and Mutton Nalli Barra are excellent choices. In dessert Kanufa is a winner.

featured_reviews.name: Sunil Kamat
featured_reviews.review_text: Ordered their Tikka Biryani. Honestly the rice and masala was classic ! But the Chicken Tikka pieces were on the dry side. Would have been a true classic if they would have been juicy.

featured_reviews.name: Svetlana Selwyn Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: This cozy restaurant can host 30 to 40 people. We had lunch here and left quite pleased with our experience. They offer valet service for convenience. The service is impressively quick, and both the quality and quantity of the food exceeded our expectations. The waiter provided excellent recommendations when we were unsure what to order. It's an affordable spot and a fantastic choice for enjoying delicious meals.

featured_reviews.name: Bashar Ahmed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Used to be a good place. Now the quality and taste is just pathetic. They don’t even cook in this branch, they get everything from their Kurla branch. Served us stale rice and chicken and didn’t even acknowledge it.

All put together, its not worth going even if their prices were reasonable. We literally couldn’t eat anything served.

featured_reviews.name: Gaurav Dixit
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good experience. We went for late dinner and my friend who is visiting with me from Bangkok.
It wasn't that busy and we ordered. We asked for suggestions and they said Lamb chop and some biryani.

After sometime he came back and said lamb isn't available.
We said something else and we had some chicken tikka which was delicious.

For the biryani, i felt he cheated as it tasted like butter chicken and rice and it was probably made last minute.

It tasted good. Maybe it's how they make it but I feel like that.

customer_updates.name: Yogesh Sharma
customer_updates.text:
South Indian food isn't all idlis and dosas and I'm happy to see a few restaurants such as The Tanjore Tiffin Room that's here to prove this point.

The Jackfruit Cutlet and Sweet Potato Yellow Chilli are great appetizers. I prefer the cutlet more owing to the interesting tangy chutney that's served with it.

We were planning to directly order the main course but our server suggested that we first sample their offerings in the form of a tasting platter. Definitely go for the tasting platter which is provided to you at no cost - it's a beautiful presentation.

It was only after the tasting platter that we opted to go for the Vegetable Madras Railway Curry. The tomato and cream base paired so well with the Malabar Parotta.

Our server recommended the Lemongrass Cooler and it was a refreshing choice.

While our experience, the food, and the service were great, what surprised me was a South Indian restaurant whose Sambar was so average. That being said, multiple visits to The Tanjore Tiffin Room are in my future.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Tanjore Tiffin Room is one of the finest places in the city to enjoy authentic South Indian cuisine in a refined yet welcoming setting. From the moment you enter, the ambience sets the tone — warm, classy, and thoughtfully designed with a blend of traditional and contemporary elements. It strikes the perfect balance between being vibrant and cosy, making it ideal for both family meals and relaxed dining with friends.

The food is truly the star here. Every dish is crafted with rich, traditional flavours that reflect the culinary heritage of South India. The tasting platter is a must-try, offering a wonderful selection of signature items that allow you to sample a variety of dishes in one go. Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Another convenience is the availability of valet parking, which makes dining here hassle-free, especially during busy hours.

Overall, The Tanjore Tiffin Room delivers a delightful South Indian dining experience with great food, superb service, and charming ambience. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Sunil Kamat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good stuff indeed ! The famous Madras Railway curry (mandatory) and Ghee Roast were both good ! The Mutton cutlets were awesome ! Only thing I found out of form was the Kokam Sour punch drink - weirdly
sour !!

featured_reviews.name: Vidhi S
featured_reviews.review_text:
Grateful for friends who recommend great dishes! The Madras Railway Curry with appams is one of the most comforting meals I’ve had. Would 10/10 recommend.

Notable mentions: Vegetable Stew & Khorma. Bonus: Lemongrass Cooler

featured_reviews.name: Nive Raitz von Frentz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prettily lit entrance leading a climb of a couple of floors to the restaurant (there is a lift). At 7:30 pm, several tables were already occupied.

Nicely presented menus, friendly staff, delicious home style recipes served in chunky brass dishes, complementary colours and textures.

Small tasting bowls of curry and rice samples are a prelude to the main course. The food is heavy, so go easy on the ordering!

We had hardly finished our starters, when the main courses piled up on the table...service could be staggered slightly.

Loos are off a small landing and could be cleaner. On our way out, the entrance area had become jammed with waiting guests, a tight situation, as were the takeaway boxes, which were over-stuffed.

featured_reviews.name: Daniel Harrington
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely stunning in every way.

Fell across this place via Google maps and waited until 10pm for a table (our fault we didn't book), however it did not disappoint.

Genuinely a top 5 all time restaurant for me. The food, the service, the ambience absolutely top tier. I have never had Indian food (from any region) as flavourful. The staff explained the concept and dishes incredibly well and the taster platter to help decide what to order was so fantastic. I would recommend this to absolutely everyone who lives in or is visiting Mumbai.

Thanks for an unforgettable night.

Please open up in London!!

featured_reviews.name: Ning Zzz
featured_reviews.review_text: Good food and nice ambiance, service was rather slow but we appreciated the thought put into the curry tasting platter and the detailed description for each curry dish. Really happy with the meal 🥘

The staff was super friendly and helpful not gonna lie, been to many restaurants and the staffs of LUCKY hotel definitely stood out. Tip them if you can. featured_reviews.name: Yasmin Begum

The aroma, perfectly cooked rice, and flavorful spices make every bite absolutely satisfying.

As someone who is not a hardcore mutton lover, I was genuinely surprised by how amazing their mutton biryani tasted.

The meat was tender, juicy, and blended perfectly with the rich flavors of the biryani.

This is the perfect place for non-veg food lovers. We ordered a chicken biriyani and tandoori chicken, and both were extremely tasty. The biriyani had great masala, and the long-grain rice was cooked perfectly. I especially loved the tandoori chicken—it was very flavorful.

I visited twice, once for lunch and again the next day for breakfast. Both times, the service was excellent. I must mention Mr. Saleem, who servs near the reception area—he interacted with us very politely and made us feel welcome.

On the second day, even though the restaurant officially opens at 9 AM, we reached at 8:40 AM. One of the staff members kindly guided us to enter from the backside and served us food. That gesture truly impressed us.

featured_reviews.name: Nilesh Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited in Bandra West for lunch with friends and really enjoyed the experience. Since I don’t eat chicken, I ordered the egg biryani, and it tasted very good - definitely better than egg biryanis I have had at other places in Mumbai. The flavors were nice and not too heavy. I also tried the lassi, which was fresh and refreshing.

My friends had the chicken biryani, and they said it was one of the best biryanis they’ve eaten. The service was quick and polite, and valet parking is available, which makes things easier in a busy area like Bandra.

I would say it's a good place for a lunch with good food specially for people who loves non-veg dishes.

featured_reviews.name: heeral rathod
featured_reviews.review_text:
Lucky Restaurant is one of those places where the food is so good that your phone stays in your pocket 📵😋
We ordered Malai Chicken Tikka and Chicken Biryani, and honestly—chef’s kiss! Absolutely delicious. In veg, we tried the Vegetable Sandwich and Manchurian, which were equally satisfying.
We were so busy enjoying the food that we barely clicked any pictures—only the Chicken Malai Tikka (because it arrived first 😄) and the Caramel Custard (because desserts always deserve a photo).
The ambience and vibe were great—perfect for a relaxed and happy meal. A special shoutout to Mr. Akhatar Bhai, our server, who was extremely polite, attentive, and added to the overall pleasant experience.
Great food, great service, great time. Will definitely be coming back! 🙌🍽️

What an history of serving great food. Was expecting a Great Biriyani but it was quite good for me. But the Chicken tikka was something out of 100/10. Loved the falovour juicy tender meat . featured_reviews.name: Sahera Khatoon
featured_reviews.review_text: This was my first visit to Lucky Restaurant, and the experience turned out to be extremely poor. A hair was found in my food during the meal, and subsequently, another hair was discovered in the second dish as well. I do not believe they maintain any standards of hygiene. Furthermore, the staff's behavior is unpleasant; they seem to be judgmental, treating customers well only if they spend a significant amount of money. After all this transpired, the owner finally appeared; however, even after being apprised of the situation, he behaved quite nonchalantly—I did not sense any genuine seriousness on his part. In the end, they offered us a 20% discount. What is the point of offering a 20% discount on food that contained hair? Are you merely playing with your customers' emotions? I had previously visited the Kolkata branch of this restaurant, and the maintenance, hygiene, and food quality there were excellent. It was based on that positive experience that I decided to visit this particular branch; however, the experience here was abysmal in comparison to the Kolkata outlet. In conclusion, I would simply say this: Dear customers, please be careful.🤢🤮

Had a horrible experience at Bademiya. We waited for almost an hour for our food, and after such a long wait, the quality was extremely disappointing.

The Paneer Bhurji had more oil than paneer. It was excessively oily and impossible to enjoy. The Dal Tadka had burnt jeera tadka throughout, which completely ruined the taste and gave it a bitter burnt flavor.

The Mutton biryani is definitely a must try along with their mutton rogan ghosh.
This was the first time I’ve dined at Bademiya and I’ve become a fan of their biryani.
The service was amazing.
The restaurant staff are very polite and approachable and quick with their work.
And the ambiance of the restaurant is very delicate and soft and gives you a feel of enjoying your food royally.
The food here is definitely a must try.

featured_reviews.name: Surabhi Gujar
featured_reviews.review_text: Recently visited BadeMiya, Bandra. The ambiance is excellent—clean, well maintained, and easily 5/5. featured_reviews.name: A P
featured_reviews.review_text: We had lunch at Khane Khas at Bandra west today. First thing I noticed is that the owner Mr Chaddha gave me a warm smile as soon we entered. We started off with Aam panna- made fresh by Mr Chaddha’s mother who is 85 years of age. Perfect taste and quite refreshing. We started with MUTTON SEEKH ROLL. Juicy & tasty mutton kebab in a roll. (5/5). Then we had PUNJABI MUTTON SUKKA ( thick gravy with tender flavorful pieces of mutton - the spices were underplayed perfectly to enhance the flavor of mutton, exactly how I like it) - 5/5. The only dish which did not meet up to our expectations was the Dhuan paneer masala. The paneer was quite soft and tasty but the taste of the gravy was not put the mark. But all of that was overshadowed by the attitude and demeanor of Mr Hardeep Singh Chaddha- - very warm & humble. ( he even allowed us take a picture with him) Thanks for a great experience and will surely come back to try other dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Parimal Udapurkar
featured_reviews.review_text: This place had hands down the best service I have experienced in Mumbai. In addition to the great food, the plates were spotless, the serving of lachha pyaaz was generous, the water was served a perfect cold and the waiting staff was attentive and prompt. These things don't happen on their own without someone's attention to detail. Incredibly lucky to have dined at a place run so passionately.

featured_reviews.name: akshat singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Quite a decent restaurant to try out good north indian food. Their spice levels are good and the masala's are used in just the right quantity making the dishes delectable and sumptuous. Their tandoori is absolutely heart-warming but the dhuan chicken was not worth the hype it has.

Ambience is not too great but on a cool windy day, it's a good place. The staff is really polite and helpful. Worth a try outlet for sure.

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
Khane khas is one of those small warm places you go to in bandra for a hot desi meal.
My friend tried the dal tadka that was perfectly made, just enough for us to be  to be able to alter it to our preferences.
The butter chicken they have is just the way I like it, non sweet. It's savoury and delectable.
The garlic naan and kulcha both were nice as well. All in all a good hearty dinner.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a spot in Bandra that serves North Indian food so good, you’ll forget that you’re in Mumbai and be transported straight to Punjab. It’s called Papa Pancho Da Dhaba and they’ve got a menu that’s small and straightforward - but they do these dishes so well and in such an authentic manner - we for sure haven’t had such North Indian food in Mumbai. The Dal Makhani, Cheese Kulcha, Makhani Chicken, Kasturi Kebab, Dahi Papdi Chaat and Matka Kulfi - all of your seemingly regular dishes but here it’s all elevated, rich and very real. The interiors are colourful and very dhaba-like. If this is a cuisine you enjoy, save this spot!

featured_reviews.name: Pulastya Dave
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent experience for a family get together had yesterday for lunch.
Ordered the following:
Papa Pancho Special Chicken Tikka
Mutton Seekh Kebabs
Mutton chaap
Mutton bhuna
Chicken biryani
Dal tadka

Staff is polite and friendly & service is relatively quick.
I will certainly return to try more dishes in the future.

featured_reviews.name: Nikshay Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text: Great spot for North Indian food in Mumbai. We mostly ordered vegetarian dishes, and the Sarson da Saag with Makke di Roti was honestly so good. The service was a bit slow, but totally worth the wait.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Papa Pancho da dhaba is a kind of experience amidst the by-lanes of hype Bandra Pali Hill. You get into this colourful world of roadside dhabas as soon as you step in. Sparkly danglers, colourful patakas, slogans written on trucks decorated on the walls.
Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

featured_reviews.name: Rivha Dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Imagine a dhaba in the middle of the city and that too in Bandra!! Well got an opportunity to visit “ Papa Pancho da Dhaba” with family. Was surprised on a Thursday night, it was crowded with people waiting to be seated, that is how popular the place is.

We ordered the Tandoori Chicken which was crisp from outside and moist from inside, well spiced and really tasty.  Next was Dahi Pappi Chat, a well balanced crispy, chatpata, khatta meetha, but for the cost, the quantity could be a lil more.

In main course it was Chicken Handi with Butter Garlic Naan, served with Dal Makhni and Curd. Next was but for sure Amritsari Kulcha…. served with white butter dollop and buttery dal makhni. We were almost full, but on suggestion we ordered Chicken Dal Khichadi, which surprisingly was very comforting with bits of Chicken … we ended the meal with  Lassi… a must at any Punjabi place. A huge copper glass full!!

Biryani by kilo!
This place serves the best biryani in the city. They have various types of biryani from their wide spread menu. The ingredients that they use are of high quality and taste really good. featured_reviews.review_text: “Pathetic biryani". It felt like there was no care in preparation and it was a total waste of money. I would've personally rated below 1 star if there was an option.

featured_reviews.name: Sadhana Viswanadhuni
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a true Hyderabadi my search for such amazing biryani never ends! I hated mumbai for not having it here! But now I don't need to look any further😍😍😍
Biryani By Kilo's biryani are sooo hyderabadi in taste that one is definitely going to have a foodgasm!❤️
My search ends here today as now I'm gonna keep ordering from BBK to satisfy my biryani cravings 😍😍 We ordered for
Paneer Nawabi Curry ✨
A delectable paneer dish! The gravy was very smooth with the right amount of spices and softtt paneer 😍
Ulte Tawa ka Parantha ✨
It's like a thicker smaller version of rumali roti but much better than that! As we ordered the food earlier we heated it up on tawa and savoured it with the paneer curry 😍
Veg Hyderabadi Biryani ✨
A properly packed flavoured rice with amazingly marinated veggies! The masalas were right and yummm. What more?? They even serve it with SALAN like in Hyderabad!!!!! 😍😍😍💞
Veg Kathal Dum Biryani ✨ - MUST HAVE!!!!!!!
This delicacy of south is a seasonal favourite and I was very doubtful if it would match to my expectations and mind me it was way beyond that! It had the perfect taste like we get it back in south!
And it was a super hit with all my family members!
😍😍😍
The biryanis were served with
Onion and lemon salad
Salan and Raita too❤️

Coming to the packaging can you think of any other better eco friendly packaging?? To top it off they even provided us with an aanch lighting which allows one to place the pot on candle burner! Which is sure to keep the handi and rice in it warm and fresh😍😍😍

If the green dough sealing gets hard and tough to remove! Don't hesitate to take help of a knife! That part might be tricky but I think a good sealed bowl is very important for perfect biryani 😍🤤🤤

So happy to have stumbled upon this brand! Forever thankful for bringing Hyderabadi Biryani to Mumbai 😍😍😍😍😍😍😍

Biryani by kilo is my favorite place for biryani. Yesterday I ordered chicken Hyderabadi biryani chicken korma and ulte tave ka paratha from them.
I like their biryani a lot and I have previously ordered from them too. The packaging was very good it was spill proof and sealed with the atta they also provided another matka for reheating of biryani ,specially I loved the chicken korma so much. flavors of spices were same as I expected

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Biryani by Kilo is one of safest and trusted brand delivering quality biryanis to our doorstep.
Last Thursday we ordered some of the dishes from there. The best thing about them was they deliver biryanis in earthen pots.
Delivery was quick and on time.
The dishes we tried were :

1) Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani (5/5) : Served in a earthen pot with live heating candles. The rice was cooked well. Chicken pieces were perfectly coojed in spices. Overall the biryani was awesome.
Salan and raita was complementary with the biryani was so good.

2) Chicken Korma (5/5) : It was lil sweet as I love. Chicken cooked in thick gravy had lipsmacking flavours. It was also packed in earthern pot.

3) Ulte Tawa ka Paratha (5/5) : It was just perfect. I was trying this first time and really love it.

All the dishes were scrumptious and enough for 3 people .
Hygine and stromg packing was done to avoid spillage and contamination.
Proper safety checks were done.

They made my day, surely gonna order them again.

featured_reviews.name: Foodie Kudi ke Chatake
featured_reviews.review_text: Are you a biryani lover ? If yes then Biryani by kilo is what you should try must. Very impressed with their matka packing which is being offered with candle and a mud pot to heat thir biryani before having it. Secondly packing was excellent and food delivered was peeping hot. Also there is a chutney served along with biryani which is a perfect combination to have with their biryani. Paneer nawabi was good in taste specially the paneer pieces were very soft. Overall a good first experience with them. Will surely try their other varieties in Biryani specially.

featured_reviews.name: Priyanka Kwatra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Best Biryani ever! I love Biryani by Kilo. They have the longest, most flavourful rice in their Biryani. We love their Hyderabadi Biryani the most. It is spicy and made in masalas. It comes with delicious salan, onions and green chutney. The chicken in the biryani is nice and juicy and quantity is also quite good. The handi has to be heated for 5-7 mins before having it. It is Highly recommended to do so as it gives steamy hot well done rice in your plate and it feels we are at a restaurant.
We also had chicken korma with ulta tawa parathas. Korma was also delicious and had quite authentic taste and flavor. The paratha when heated on tawa became nice and flaky. Suggest you to do the same but not too much as it becomes too crisp.
Overall Excellent food delivery and always trustworthy for the taste and flavor. Value for money!

featured_reviews.review_text:
We had originally checked with Soul Fry for their karaoke nights, but the owner mentioned that reservations usually need to be made around 10 days to 2 weeks in advance. Later, we ended up going there for lunch on one of the days. I had even called beforehand to ask if reservations were necessary, and he said yes, definitely. But when we actually reached, the restaurant was pretty empty.

The food was good — nothing extremely standout, but overall decent. One thing we did feel though was that everything was slightly on the pricier side for what was offered. That being said, the interiors really give you that old-school Goan tavern vibe, which added a nice charm to the experience.

featured_reviews.name: george joseph
featured_reviews.review_text: What a find. A cute little restaurant with goan vibes right in bandra. You would need to plan to be there around opening time if you want to get a seat in their cozy indoor area. They close for the evening making it a little exclusive with the time restriction. The food was really good. We ordered a chicken starter along with the prawn curry rice and pork vindaloo. The prawn curry rice combo is a must try. Coming from Kerala it gave me those beach vibes. The curry is runny and just perfect with rice. It felt just like it was made at home. The pork was incredible. The pieces they had in the vindaloo consisted of fat and flesh you always die for. Not a lot of places get this right. It was a little too sweet for my usual vindaloo but nonetheless tasty. We could not get an inside sitting spot but consider yourself lucky if you do. I'm sure the experience would be worth it. One of the best places i have visited in bandra.

featured_reviews.name: Ashwinth Naveen
featured_reviews.review_text: My first time in Mumbai, and I have absolutely no regrets choosing Soul Fry as my go-to spot! The karaoke night was an absolute blast and made the whole experience even more memorable. The vibe, music, and overall atmosphere were amazing, and I genuinely had such a great time. Definitely one of the highlights of my trip — would love to visit again!

featured_reviews.name: Raj doesn't share food
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Veranda around 4 PM, and the first thing to note is that the kitchen was partially closed at that time, which limited a few options. Still, we managed to order a decent variety of dishes.
We tried prawns thecha, chicken 65, chicken tenders, pizza, pasta, and Hakka noodles. Most of the food was actually good and enjoyable. The highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns thecha, easily the best dish on the table. It was flavorful, well-cooked, and something I’d genuinely go back for.
The pizza and pasta were nice, chicken 65 was solid, and overall the food quality was pretty satisfying. But the Hakka noodles were a letdown. They had a strong smell, likely from the egg and chicken, which made it hard to enjoy the dish.
Another downside was the timing of the chicken tenders. They arrived way too late, almost after we were done eating everything else, which kind of ruined the flow of the meal.
That said, the ambience is where Veranda really stands out. The place looks amazing, has a great vibe, and the location is perfect for a chill outing in Bandra.
Overall, it’s a good place with great ambience and mostly good food, but a few issues with timing and consistency in dishes hold it back slightly.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve ordered from Carter’s Blue many times, and I probably get their chicken shawarma around three times a week. The reason I keep coming back is simple — the shawarma is honestly one of the best in town. The flavor, the filling, and the overall taste are consistently great, and it’s definitely the highlight of this place.

However, I’ve had some frustrating experiences with delivery and service. My building requires the delivery person to call when they arrive so the watchman can confirm and allow them in. Because of this, the staff sometimes say it “wastes time,” even though my house is literally less than a minute away from the restaurant.

Once, they told me the delivery person had already left for another order. To check if that was actually true, I placed another order from a different building right in front of mine. It turned out the delivery person hadn’t gone anywhere, which was disappointing because I’m a regular customer and it felt like they just didn’t want to take the extra minute to deliver.

Another small annoyance is when you walk past the restaurant. Staff often stand outside pushing menus and calling out repeatedly, which can feel a bit overwhelming when you’re just passing by.

I would also suggest improving hygiene standards. On one occasion I saw someone handling the food in a way that didn’t look very sanitary, which is concerning for any food place.

That said, I can’t deny that the food itself is excellent, especially the shawarma. If they improved their service, delivery attitude, and hygiene practices, this place could easily be even better.

Overall: Amazing shawarma, but service and hygiene definitely need improvement.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My recent home delivery from Joseph kitchen Tandoori Bandra left me utterly disappointed and disgusted. I cannot emphasize enough how atrocious my experience was at this so-called restaurant. From the moment I walked through the door until the bitter end, it was a relentless parade of disappointment and frustration.

Let's start with the ambiance. The place was a complete disaster. The dim lighting attempted to hide the filth and grime that covered every inch of the restaurant. The tables were sticky, the chairs were worn-out, and the overall atmosphere reeked of stale air and desperation. It felt like stepping into a time capsule from the '70s, but without any charm or nostalgia.

The service was an absolute nightmare. The staff seemed disinterested and disengaged, barely acknowledging my presence. It took an eternity to even get a menu, and once I finally managed to place my order, the waiting game began. The food took an eternity to arrive, and when it did, it was clear that they had completely forgotten about any notion of quality or taste.

The food itself was downright atrocious. The menu promised culinary delights, but what I received was a sad excuse for a meal. The ingredients were subpar, clearly of the lowest quality available. The presentation resembled a toddler's art project, with haphazard plating and a complete lack of finesse. And as for the taste, it was an assault on my palate. The flavors were bland, uninspired, and in some cases, downright repulsive. I wouldn't be surprised if the ingredients were pulled from the dumpster behind the restaurant.

To add insult to injury, the prices were exorbitant for the abysmal quality offered. I would have been better off throwing my money into a bonfire. The bill left me in disbelief, questioning my life choices and wondering how such a terrible establishment could have the audacity to charge such astronomical prices.

In conclusion, I strongly advise everyone to steer clear of Joseph’s Tandoori kitchen unless you have an insatiable desire to be utterly disappointed. From the lackluster ambiance to the abysmal service and the dreadful food, this restaurant is a prime example of everything that can go wrong in the culinary world. Spare yourself the misery and find a better place to dine or order.

The Star: Fried Fish with Pav

The Fried Fish here is iconic—perfectly seasoned, crispy on the outside, and flaky within. But the real game-changer is pairing it with the Mumbai Pav. There is something about the texture and flavor of a local Mumbai pav that just hits differently; it’s the ultimate vessel for the spicy fish, especially when you load it up with their signature green chutney and crunchy onions. It’s a simple combination, but it's a "Mumbaikar" soul-food experience

The Sides & Mains
• Prawns Crispy: These lived up to the name. Golden, crunchy, and packed with flavor, they are the perfect appetizer to snack on while you soak in the Bandra energy

• Chicken Tawa Biryani: To wrap things up, the Chicken Tawa Biryani is a must-try. Unlike traditional dum biryanis, the tawa style gives it a unique, rustic smoky flavor and a spice profile that is bold and satisfying.

The Verdict
Eating here isn't just about the food; it's about the "Bliss of Taste." If you want to eat like a true Mumbaikar, grabbing a plate of fish and pav at Jai Jawan is an absolute rite of passage.

Highly Recommended for: Seafood lovers and anyone craving an authentic taste of Mumbai’s street-side culinary excellence.

Small sitting but service is super fast and turn around table is that like always waiting customers in big rush.

All the best team JJ.

Regards!

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Londhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Jai Jawan, Bandra

I recently visited Jai Jawan with my friends after a movie, mainly because we had seen and heard a lot about the place through Instagram reels. Since we were already in Bandra, we decided to give it a try. We reached the restaurant around 9:00 PM, which is peak dinner time, and had to wait for nearly 20 minutes to get a table for four—which was understandable considering the rush.

Once seated, we ordered Chicken Tikka Masala and Chicken Tandoori as starters. The starters were okayish in taste, nothing impressive. I assume this might have been due to the restaurant working at full capacity during peak hours.

For the main course, we ordered Butter Chicken with Rumali Rotis. Unfortunately, this was the biggest disappointment of the night. I’ve had butter chicken at countless restaurants, and honestly, this was the worst butter chicken I’ve had so far—lacking flavor, richness, and balance. We also ordered Chicken Fried Rice, which again was just average.

The service experience further added to the disappointment. There was a shortage of waiters, resulting in long waiting times for food. The staff seemed extremely busy and didn’t really have the time to listen properly to customer requests or feedback.

Another thing that stood out negatively was the entertainment setup. The restaurant has two large TV screens, but they were continuously playing the same 5-minute loop video of a Japanese city. On that particular day, there was an India cricket match, and playing it on at least one screen would have kept customers engaged—especially since food service was delayed.

Overall, I personally regret choosing Jai Jawan that night and feel I could have had a better experience elsewhere. This is purely my personal opinion. You may still try it once to form your own view, but my experience was not a good one.

This is my first time visiting India, and I’m so glad we found this gem. The Owner/Chef is incredibly welcoming; he personally helped us order and explained the flavors with such passion.

That’s exactly the kind of day I found Bombay Curry and honestly I’m so glad I did. This place feels so homely. It’s the kind of place you go to on a random night when you’ve had a bad day, you’re tired and you just want something that feels like home.

We ordered butter chicken, garlic naan and seekh kebab and every single thing was a straight 10/10. The butter chicken was rich and comforting, the garlic naan was soft and perfect and the seekh kebabs were juicy and full of flavour.

What makes it even more special is knowing that the chefs are from Lucknow and Rajasthan because you can genuinely taste that authenticity in the food. And the chef/owner himself was easily one of the most friendly and nicest chefs I’ve ever met. Warm, welcoming and clearly cooking with a lot of love. Bombay Curry feels like a hug on a plate.

We reached the hotel around 3:45 PM, just before closing time, which meant our order was taken in a bit of a hurry. We patiently waited for the food, and that’s where the experience truly took a turn for the better.

Butter Chicken Factory in Bandra is a haven for butter chicken enthusiasts. The restaurant's rendition of this classic dish is a delightful symphony of flavors – the chicken is perfectly marinated, the creamy tomato-based gravy strikes a harmonious balance of spice and sweetness. Each bite is a journey for the senses, a true culinary delight.

Sujeet's service adds a personal touch to the dining experience, ensuring a memorable visit. The mocktails, especially Pudeena Pani and Masala Shikanje, provide a refreshing start to the meal.

The Kabab Platter showcases a variety of both vegetarian and non-vegetarian delights. From the succulent Paneer Tikka to the flavorful Chicken Seekh Kebab, the assortment caters to diverse preferences.

Moving on to the mains, the Butter Chicken steals the show with its rich and decadent texture. Complemented by Butter Paneer and Dal Makhani, the restaurant offers a fulfilling array of choices.

The Bread Basket, featuring Chilli Garlic Laccha Paratha, Tandoori Roti, Pudina Paratha, and Churchur Naan, provides the perfect accompaniment to soak up the flavorful gravies. Rice lovers are not forgotten, as the restaurant offers a satisfying selection.

The meal concludes on a sweet note with Gulab Jamun, leaving diners with a lingering sweetness that perfectly caps off the gastronomic journey. Butter Chicken Factory in Bandra is undeniably a go-to spot for those seeking an authentic and indulgent butter chicken experience in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text:
This place by the Bawa Hotels Group is a good option if you’re in the mood for Punjabi food, just don’t walk in expecting completely authentic flavours. The taste is slightly toned down, but if you set your expectations right, you’ll actually enjoy the food.

The menu is quite well done, and the meal box options are a big plus. Makes ordering super easy without having to overthink or pick too many individual items.

Their parathas are definitely worth trying—served nicely with curd. Do ask for white butter separately though, as it’s not given by default and really makes a difference. The lassi is a must-have here, easily one of the better things on the menu.

Also, a special mention for the Kalimiri chicken shorba. It’s not on the menu, but if they have it, don’t miss it—it’s genuinely very good.

Ambience is nice and comfortable, so no complaints there. Service, however, is quite slow and needs serious improvement, which can get a bit frustrating.

Parking is another issue—since it’s close to the railway station, the area is always crowded and finding a spot is tough. Better to plan that in advance.

Overall, a good place to chill and enjoy a meal, as long as you’re okay overlooking the service and parking hassles.

Here’s a full review in your signature tone, covering the Torii experience:

⸻

Torii, Bandra – Big on Vibe, Big on Bill, Bigger on Taste

When your group of diners ranges from sushi scholars to soy sauce dabblers, you need a place that checks all boxes. Torii in Bandra came highly recommended—and spoiler alert—it almost lives up to the hype, and then some.

Let’s start from the outside: that black-and-white arched entrance with the gold-lettered TORII feels like you’re about to enter a movie set. Inside, the vibe is unmistakably plush—with mirrored ceilings, retro lampshades, opulent seating, and music that doesn’t scream at you but keeps the energy flowing. It’s where Japanese zen meets Mumbai glam.

The Meal
We were 7. The table bill read ₹45,999, so yes, about ₹6.5K per head after taxes and service, but here’s what made it feel worth it:
•	Cold Young Coconut Carpaccio – Sounds fancy and tasted the part. Light, tropical, and a perfect start.
•	Miso Black Cod – Showstopper dish. Silky, melt-in-mouth. It’s what black cod dreams are made of.
•	Chicken Chilli Oil & Lemongrass Chicken Tsukune – Packed flavour bombs. The chilli oil was a standout.
•	Cold Prawns Tempura Maki – Crisp, clean, and a hit with everyone at the table.
•	Twilight Tingles (mocktail) – Refreshing and not sugary, a tough balance to nail.
•	Torii X-mess Sundae – The name may be cheeky, but this dessert brought childlike joy with its waffle castle presentation. The kind of ending you photograph before devouring.

Service
Smooth, attentive, and non-intrusive. Our server knew the menu well and paced the meal right. That’s half the job done in high-end dining.

What Could Be Better?
Not much honestly. A couple of small hits and misses on portion sizes (looking at you, gyoza), but hey, we weren’t here for the quantity.
The bill might jolt you for a second, but by the end of the night, you’ll justify it to yourself with, “Well, the black cod made up for it.”

My final two bit

Paise gaye, par taste ban gaya.

Aide  dessert  pe toh calories bhi selfie mangti hai.

📍 Final Verdict:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ — A strong 5 stars for a place that brings together design, service, and standout dishes under one gilded roof. For special dinners, date nights, or flex-worthy Instagram reels, Torii hits the spot..

featured_reviews.name: rajesh jaiswar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kari Apla is one of those rare restaurants that immediately makes you feel at home the moment you step inside. It’s a small, warm space in Khar with a simple, earthy charm — the kind of place where you can actually hear conversations, enjoy the aroma from the open kitchen, and feel connected to the food being prepared.

The menu is a beautiful mix of coastal, Kerala, and Maharashtrian flavours, but presented in a very thoughtful and modern way. Every dish has a story, and you can sense the amount of care the chefs put into balancing comfort with creativity. The curries are rich without being heavy, the spices are well-rounded, and the seafood is exceptionally fresh. Even the vegetarian dishes stand out with bold, homely flavours.

Their weekend brunch is especially worth trying — soft appams, dosas, light stews, filter coffee — everything tastes like a regional home kitchen brought into a modern dining space. Portions are satisfying and plating is elegant without being overdone.

Service is polite, patient, and genuinely interested in helping you choose. Because the space is compact, the whole experience feels personal and relaxed rather than rushed or commercial.

Prices are on the higher side, but completely justified considering the quality, originality, and the chef-driven approach. It’s not a “quick meal” type of place — it’s somewhere you go to slow down and enjoy food with intention.

Overall: Kari Apla is a wonderful blend of nostalgia, regional flavours, and modern presentation. If you enjoy coastal Indian cuisine or simply love trying thoughtfully crafted food, this is a spot you shouldn’t miss.

Recently I visited Miya Kebab and I absolutely loved the food there. The place has some really unique and flavorful dishes.

I tried Mutton Kheema Hummus, Changezi Chicken Tikka, Kashmiri Chicken Tikka, and an Angara Chicken Shawarma. The highlight for me was the Zadran Naan served with hummus. The naan was full of flavor and had cheese inside, which made it taste amazing with the hummus. It was such a nice fusion and something different from the usual.

Both the Changezi Chicken Tikka and Kashmiri Chicken Tikka had a very rich taste with great smoky flavors. The Angara Shawarma was also one of the best shawarmas I’ve had.
However, the service could definitely be improved. The staff took quite a long time to serve the food and there seemed to be some internal miscommunication, so they couldn’t give an approximate waiting time. Also, there is no proper parking available nearby.
Overall, the food quality and taste were excellent, and I would definitely visit again for the flavors, but better service and parking arrangements would make the experience even better.
